newsitem.title: USA: Calif.'s credit improves,localities regress - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif.'s credit improves,localities regress - report.

text.p: The financial condition of the state of California is improving but local governments still face major fiscal obstacles, according to a report on state finances.
John Nuveen & Co Inc said in a report that California state government has benefited from the state's economic turnaround as revenues have increased and fund deficits have declined.
Nuveen warned, however, that the state has not established a long-term capital program "in-line with the requirements dictated by forecasts of expansive long-term growth."

Nuveen said "considerably more spending" would be needed in order to get prison capacity to more reasonable levels. In addition, Nuveen said the state's general maintenance of highway roads appears to be "vastly underfunded."
While this year's proposed budget is "more county friendly" than prior year budget plans, the John Nuveen report warned that local governments still face challenges.
"State credit continues to improve while local governments regress," John Nuveen said in the report.
"Local government financing, while not a state problem, is a problem of the state," the report concluded.
"Financial demands and restrictions enacted via voter referendums will continue to challenge the local units financial autonomy," the report said.
